llm.summary: This is mostly a coherent personal knowledge manager, but it under-discloses privacy-relevant behavior in its visualization and persistent data handling.

dimensions.detail: Local filesystem use is purpose-aligned and documented through memory/ storage plus Desktop visualization output, but the generated visualization's remote script load conflicts with the stated no-network privacy boundary.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The README recommends mutable installation commands, including npx clawhub@latest and an unpinned git clone, so future installed code may differ from the reviewed artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions are mostly user-directed CLI/API actions and do not show prompt hijacking or hidden role changes. Mutating commands such as add, link, auto-adjust, synthesis, and prune are expected for this skill, but their effects should be more explicitly labeled as persistent and, for prune, destructive.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists personal concepts, beliefs, search-hit usage logs, SQLite state, and plaintext JSON files; this is central to the purpose, but prune can permanently delete deprecated concepts, links, usage logs, and JSON files without an interactive confirmation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core purpose matches the artifacts: storing, searching, linking, distilling, and visualizing personal concepts and beliefs. The concern is that the visualization claims a local-only security model while loading remote D3 JavaScript, and the HTML rendering path has unsafe data embedding/rendering patterns if user knowledge reaches the template.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing. It stores personal knowledge, beliefs, contexts, and search usage in local plaintext files and SQLite; use --dry-run before prune and avoid putting highly sensitive material into the visualization until the remote D3 dependency is vendored or pinned and the HTML rendering is hardened. Prefer pinned installer versions or reviewed commits instead of mutable latest/head commands.
llm.findings:
[T03] unexpected: Confirmed: viz-template.html loads https://d3js.org/d3.v7.min.js without pinning or integrity. Visualization is purpose-aligned, but remote executable JavaScript is not consistent with the skill's local-only/no-network claim.
[T09] unexpected: Partially supported: visualize.py inserts raw JSON into an HTML/JavaScript context in its fallback path and the template renders tags with innerHTML. The shipped template currently lacks the GRAPH_DATA_PLACEHOLDER, reducing normal-path exploitability, but the coding pattern is still unsafe for private user knowledge.
[T08] unexpected: Confirmed as an installation-risk note: the README uses mutable npx and git instructions. No malicious package behavior was observed inside the reviewed artifact itself.
[SDI-1] expected: Pruning low-value knowledge is within the stated feature set and the SKILL.md example uses --dry-run, but the non-dry-run path permanently deletes local records and files without confirmation or backup.
[SQP-2] expected: Persistent SQLite/JSON storage and search-hit logging are expected for a knowledge engine and are partly disclosed, but plaintext sensitive beliefs/search history and destructive mutations deserve clearer up-front warnings.
[P6] unexpected: Not supported by artifact evidence: the cited 'return rules' code returns reflection-rule data, not system prompts or hidden instructions.
[TT2] expected: The JSON card writes are expected local persistence. The reviewed card paths are built from fixed memory directories and sanitized generated IDs; the cited environment-taint claim was not supported for those card_path writes.
[LP3] unexpected: Local file access is required, but the skill does not declare a tight writable boundary beyond documentation. This is an under-scoping concern rather than evidence of abuse.
[SQP-3] expected: The Chinese-only documentation, CLI text, schemas, and visualization labels are overt in the artifacts. This limits audience/usability but is not by itself a security concern.
[SDI-2] expected: The eval capability is documented in SKILL.md and implemented as eval_knowledge_engine.py using a temporary test database, so it is not purpose-mismatched.
